fatal_errors: The proposed LPBF intervention does not reconstruct the reported liquid-metal dealloying of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
It treats the starting material as an existing W–Cu composite rather than a single-BCC WTaVTi alloy whose Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels are selectively replaced by Cu.
It omits the bicontinuous RHEA–Cu architecture and the approximately 300 nm W-rich passivating interlayer that are central to the reported interface stability.

The mechanism incorrectly centers on rapid solidification suppressing diffusion and invokes improved phonon transport in a metallic W–Cu system, rather than selective Ti–Cu exchange, immiscibility of W/Ta/V with Cu, interfacial W enrichment, and aligned Cu conduction pathways.
No prior evidence is supplied for the claimed 10–15% conductivity enhancement or irradiation performance.
explanation: The hypothesis broadly addresses thermal transport and interfacial defects in W/Cu joining and proposes a reasonably falsifiable matched-processing comparison. However, it misses the target material, intervention, processing conditions, structural mediator, and mechanism. The reported work used liquid-metal dealloying to convert directionally segregated WTaVTi into an aligned RHEA–Cu composite, not LPBF processing of W–Cu. It also fails to reproduce the temperature-dependent thermal result, including roughly 75 W m−1 K−1 at room temperature, approximately 140 W m−1 K−1 at 800 °C, and crossover above pure W near 650 °C. Irradiation boundaries are left unspecified, whereas the target evidence was limited to 25 keV He+ screening of precursor dendrites as a proxy rather than direct irradiation of the completed composite. Although the proposed experiment could test the LPBF claim, absence of supporting evidence and the questionable transport mechanism make this an unsupported alternative rather than a reconstruction.
